# About the Author {.unnumbered}

Vijay Janapa Reddi is the Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical and Computer
Engineering at Harvard University. His research spans computer architecture,
runtime systems, edge computing, and machine-learning systems, with a
longstanding focus on co-design across hardware, software, systems, and machine
learning. Much of that work examines the interfaces among these layers, where a
hardware decision changes the software and runtime choices available, and those
choices change the system-level performance and efficiency tradeoffs.

He has also worked to make machine-learning performance claims measurable and
reproducible. As a founding board member of MLCommons, he helped build the
MLPerf benchmark program spanning data-center systems and embedded machine
learning.

That perspective shapes *Architecture 2.0*. The book asks when AI assistance
improves a computer system, how that improvement should be measured and checked,
and what the evidence allows an architect to decide.
